files.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: ORIGINAL opaque 1024 x 1536 portrait scrolling terrain tile for chapter 4 of an anime aerial shooter.
Input images: Image 1 is ONLY the approved hand-painted anime environment style and overhead scale reference (the green island), not its sea/grass/radar subject or layout. Image 2 is ONLY the chapter's EXISTING sewer/drainage theme reference: teal murky water, old concrete, small rusted pipes, damp moss and maintenance platforms; DO NOT copy its huge pipes, tall walls, black center or close low perspective.
Primary request: recreate this industrial drainage canal district with the same soft painterly brush texture, clear broad shapes and connected terrain as reference 1. It must feel viewed from a HIGH-FLYING aircraft. Near-overhead orthographic bird's-eye view, about 80 degrees downward from the horizon; mostly roofs and ground, only SHORT shallow embankment faces and small wall sides. No horizon, ceiling, tunnel cross-section or tilted isometric diorama.
Scene: a continuous broad industrial waterway with varied low concrete embankments, small service islands and side filter basins. Quiet deep desaturated blue-green/teal water occupies about 50–60% and flows in an irregular gently curving main channel through the central half. Do NOT create a straight narrow trench between two continuous vertical walls. Banks stagger asymmetrically and widen into maintenance yards. Use clear slate-gray concrete, modest brown rust and small restrained moss patches. Keep subdued midtone daylight; damp atmosphere but readable, not grim black or filthy brown. Main channel has subtle broken painted reflections, not ocean surf or neon acid, and the central 45% is visually quiet for bullets.
Scale: this canvas covers a wide DISTRICT, with 8–12 small distinct maintenance structures across the full image. Small low pump/control buildings have roof widths 25–55 pixels; low service yards about 60–110 pixels, pipe diameters mostly 4–9 pixels. No gigantic pipe framing the image and no enormous bridge. Small ladders, valves, drains, concrete joints, grates, a few crates and scattered curb rubble provide scale, only where plausible. Every structure sits on a contiguous founded platform with contact shadow and a connected access path. Pipe supports touch the banks; drainage outlets visibly join canal water with small short water plumes. No floating sticker objects. NO radar, satellite dish, lighthouse or forest copied from image 1.
Lighting: diffuse daylight from UPPER RIGHT, all shadows cast LOWER LEFT. Cool desaturated teal water with warm gray concrete highlights, dull green-gray and rusty copper pipes, restrained warm yellow service markings. Broad visible painterly strokes and a few crisp functional edges, not a photographic texture, hard plastic 3D render, heavy black outlines or smeared dirty wash.
Vertical tile edges: at BOTH the exact top and bottom edge the main quiet teal water channel is centered at x=54% width and is about 36% of image width, with low irregular concrete bank strips continuing through both ends. Same water hue and scale at both ends for directional scrolling. Natural texture continues to the edges; no broad horizontal roadway, full-width dam, empty separator band or border. Place focal buildings away from the top/bottom 5%. No large water splash or important object cropped at the seam.
Constraints: NO clouds, fog veil, steam, smoke, screen-space particles or vignetting baked into this terrain; atmosphere is a separate game layer. No aircraft, characters, enemies, projectiles, UI, labels, readable text, logos, watermark, frame, checkerboard or transparent gaps. No sci-fi neon sludge and no sky. Keep the industrial drainage identity; no lush island/coast conversion.
Layout A — pumping station: an irregular stepped maintenance yard at mid-left supports two different small low-roof pump/control sheds, a few anchored copper-gray pipe runs and a small squared settling basin. Lower-right has a low concrete spillway with two short round drainage outlets and a tiny service shed. The main channel bends gently left then right with broad calm patches. A few broken low curb edges and damp moss soften the otherwise functional concrete forms. Do not fill the center with structures.
